Subject: Temporary cross-border processing during EU maintenance window

Tessa —

We're preparing for a scheduled platform maintenance in our EU region the weekend of Feb 21–22. Our procurement and security teams asked whether Redwood can support a short-term exception that allows sessions to be processed in the US region only for the duration of the maintenance (expected ~6 hours), while retaining EU residency guarantees the rest of the time.

Primary asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether region pinning can be temporarily relaxed for a subset of sessions?
- What exact data would transit US infrastructure (request/response payload, KV cache, logs)?
- How do you guarantee auditability and ability to restrict retention for those transient sessions?
- Which subprocessors would be involved if processing leaves EU?

Procurement asked for a short exception template/DPA addendum we can review. We need this clarified to complete approvals by Feb 12.

Appreciate a quick rundown and any docs you can attach.

Best,
Jules Martin
Head of Data Privacy, FinCo Payments
jules.martin@finco.com

Hi Jules —

Thanks for the clear summary. We've looped in Marcus (runtime) and Priyom (compliance/PS) to give a succinct, actionable answer and a draft exception we can attach. Short answers up front:

- Yes — we support time-bound routing exceptions for customer sessions. The normal pin-by-customer policy remains in place; we can create a scoped routing exception that routes a defined token/route set to the US for a defined window (start/end + TTL).
- Payloads: request + generated tokens are proxied; KV cache is kept in-region whenever possible. For the short exception there are two options (see Marcus' note): transient processing where only inference execution happens in the US and ephemeral logs are captured but retained only under the exception policy, or full failover where more artifacts may transit.
- Audit/retention: we can publish an auditable event log with an 'exception-id' and case timeline. Retention can be explicitly limited in the addendum (we typically allow 0–90 days override per exception).
- Subprocessors: primary cloud provider in the US region will be involved for compute; no new third-party analytics subprocessors are introduced by default. We'll list exact subprocessor locations in the addendum.

Attached: region-exception-template.docx (draft addendum), transient-processing-specs.pdf (technical summary).

Can you share: estimated request volume during the window, whether you need KV cache affinity for certain customers, and whether logs must be excluded from any analytics exports?

If it helps, I'm available for a 30-min call today or tomorrow to walk through the template and timeline.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive

Subject: Re: Temporary cross-border processing during EU maintenance window — technical detail

Hi Jules/Tessa —

Technical notes to make the options concrete:

1) Scoped routing exception (recommended)
   - Scope: route by customer_id or route_tag for specific API keys.
   - Duration: explicit start/end + TTL (we mark every token with exception-id).
   - Data movement: inference compute will run on US-hosted instances; request/response payloads transit TLS to the US.
   - KV cache: we can configure 'cache-affinity' so any persistent keys stay in EU; only transient working set for the session is allowed to materialize in US for the exception window.

2) Failover mode (only if you need seamless availability across regions)
   - More objects may replicate temporarily. We do not recommend unless necessary.

Logging & audit
- Audit events for exception-id are generated at request start and end.
- We can enforce a retention override (e.g., drop detailed request logs after X days, keep metadata for Y days).
- Access to raw payload logs can be restricted to named contacts (we will add an access control list in the addendum).

Subprocessors
- During the exception, compute uses our US GPU pool (CloudProvider-US-1). Storage (ephemeral) is hosted in the same region; persistent storage remains in EU unless failover replication is enabled.
- No analytics/vendor subprocessors will process the raw payloads; audit and metrics collectors are EU-based by default.

Security controls
- All transit uses TLS1.3; payloads at rest use AES-256.
- If you require customer-managed keys (KMS), we can use an EU key escrow pattern and issue short-term wrapping keys for the exception window.

I attached a simple routing-fallback-diagram.png that illustrates the flow. Operationally we recommend: (a) test on a low-volume route, (b) set TTL=24h for the first run, and (c) set retention for raw logs to 7 days unless you request shorter.

Happy to discuss more on the call.

—Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
attachments: routing-fallback-diagram.png
